question: Who competes with BSP for home-services deals?
html:
Home-Services Deal Competitors

Residential services is BSP's most crowded deal market. Well-funded national consolidators set add-on prices, and several sponsor-backed companies are buying in or next to Punctual Pros' Central PA/NJ counties (Private-equity landscape).

Local and national bidders

TierCompanies / sponsorsCredit position
PA/NJ, activeSila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy Service Partners/HL Bowman (Gridiron), Ally Services (Watchtower), Northwinds (TruArc)Legacy borrows at par; Sila looks healthier than most local rivals
Local operatorHaller (Lancaster, 254 trucks)Described as healthier
National, scaledApex (Alpine), Wrench (LGP), Redwood (Altas)S+425–475, marked at par, delayed-draw lines for acquisitions
National, stressedTurnPoint (OMERS), Any Hour (Knox Lane), Len the Plumber, HorizonPart PIK interest, marked 89–94
Other nationalT3 (Riverside)Not reported

Sources: Private-equity landscape; Competitor filings.

Size gap

  • Sila has 2,500+ employees. That implies est. $450–650M revenue (low confidence). Its growth came almost entirely from acquisitions (Competitor filings).
  • Wrench is est. $1.5–2.0B revenue (low confidence) (Competitor filings).
  • BSP's main fund reports $335M sold. Rival flagships include Gridiron V at $2.1B and Trivest VII at $950M (Private-equity landscape; BSP firm profile).
  • MidOcean has the closest sector taxonomy among fund-level peers, including franchise services (Private-equity landscape).

Bidders likely to pull back

  • Horizon Services has at least $211M of first-lien debt at Blue Owl. It pays 3.75% PIK, is marked at 92.5, and its lenders hold its common equity (Competitor filings).
  • The case studies describe Horizon as lender-owned by 2026 (Home-services company case studies).
  • Heartland's debt matures Dec 15, 2026.
  • Both companies are more likely to sell assets or restructure than to bid hard for add-ons. Their branches could become targets (est.).

How BSP can compete

  • Avoid auctions.
  • Use the franchise-system angle: Authority Brands territory rights and brand conversion.
  • Run proprietary outreach to shops under $3M EBITDA, which large-cap sponsors skip (Private-equity landscape).
  • The landscape does not report win/loss data or add-on multiples by bidder. A log of lost Punctual Pros processes, with price and winning buyer, would show who actually outbids BSP.

Next actions

  1. Build a target list from Horizon and Heartland branches near Punctual Pros' counties ahead of the Dec 15, 2026 maturity.
  2. Start a deal log for Punctual Pros add-ons: bidder, price and outcome for every process seen.
  3. Confirm with Authority Brands which territory rights and conversion economics BSP can offer sellers.
  4. Map sub-$3M EBITDA HVAC/plumbing shops in Central PA/NJ that Sila, Legacy and Ally have not yet approached.

# Home-Services Deal Competitors

Residential services is BSP's most crowded deal market. Well-funded national consolidators set add-on prices, and several sponsor-backed companies are buying in or next to Punctual Pros' Central PA/NJ counties (Private-equity landscape).

## Local and national bidders

| Tier | Companies / sponsors | Credit position |
|---|---|---|
| PA/NJ, active | Sila (Goldman Sachs), Legacy Service Partners/HL Bowman (Gridiron), Ally Services (Watchtower), Northwinds (TruArc) | Legacy borrows at par; Sila looks healthier than most local rivals |
| Local operator | Haller (Lancaster, 254 trucks) | Described as healthier |
| National, scaled | Apex (Alpine), Wrench (LGP), Redwood (Altas) | S+425–475, marked at par, delayed-draw lines for acquisitions |
| National, stressed | TurnPoint (OMERS), Any Hour (Knox Lane), Len the Plumber, Horizon | Part PIK interest, marked 89–94 |
| Other national | T3 (Riverside) | Not reported |

Sources: Private-equity landscape; Competitor filings.

## Size gap

- Sila has 2,500+ employees. That implies est. $450–650M revenue (low confidence). Its growth came almost entirely from acquisitions (Competitor filings).
- Wrench is est. $1.5–2.0B revenue (low confidence) (Competitor filings).
- BSP's main fund reports $335M sold. Rival flagships include Gridiron V at $2.1B and Trivest VII at $950M (Private-equity landscape; BSP firm profile).
- MidOcean has the closest sector taxonomy among fund-level peers, including franchise services (Private-equity landscape).

## Bidders likely to pull back

- Horizon Services has at least $211M of first-lien debt at Blue Owl. It pays 3.75% PIK, is marked at 92.5, and its lenders hold its common equity (Competitor filings).
- The case studies describe Horizon as lender-owned by 2026 (Home-services company case studies).
- Heartland's debt matures Dec 15, 2026.
- Both companies are more likely to sell assets or restructure than to bid hard for add-ons. Their branches could become targets (est.).

## How BSP can compete

- Avoid auctions.
- Use the franchise-system angle: Authority Brands territory rights and brand conversion.
- Run proprietary outreach to shops under $3M EBITDA, which large-cap sponsors skip (Private-equity landscape).
- The landscape does not report win/loss data or add-on multiples by bidder. A log of lost Punctual Pros processes, with price and winning buyer, would show who actually outbids BSP.

## Next actions

1. Build a target list from Horizon and Heartland branches near Punctual Pros' counties ahead of the Dec 15, 2026 maturity.
2. Start a deal log for Punctual Pros add-ons: bidder, price and outcome for every process seen.
3. Confirm with Authority Brands which territory rights and conversion economics BSP can offer sellers.
4. Map sub-$3M EBITDA HVAC/plumbing shops in Central PA/NJ that Sila, Legacy and Ally have not yet approached.
